description_full: Healthcare Services Group, Inc. provides management, administrative, and operating services to the housekeeping, laundry, linen, facility maintenance, and dietary service departments of nursing homes, retirement complexes, rehabilitation centers, and hospitals in the United States. The company operates in two segments, Environmental Services and Dietary. Its Environmental Services segment engages in cleaning, disinfecting, and sanitizing of resident rooms and common areas of the customers' facilities, as well as the laundering and processing of the bed linens, uniforms, resident personal clothing, and other assorted linen items utilized at the customers' facilities. The Dietary segment is involved in the management of the customers' dietary departments, which focus on food purchasing, meal preparation, and professional dietitian services, such as the development of menus that meet the dietary needs of residents; and the provision of on-site management and clinical consulting services. It also offers provides hospitality and support services. The company serves long-term and post-acute care facilities, hospitals, and the healthcare industry through referrals and solicitation of target facilities. Healthcare Services Group, Inc. was incorporated in 1976 and is headquartered in Bensalem, Pennsylvania.

financial_summary: Healthcare Services Group, Inc. is a small-cap healthcare business with a $1.7B market cap on $1.8B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +3% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, which puts it in mature, slow-growth territory.
Returns on capital run at 10% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business barely earns its keep economically.

The business throws off $139M in free cash flow — roughly 8 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders, and cash conversion sits at 2.45× so those profits are backed by real cash.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage of 41× is fortress-like.

Shareholder yield of 3.7% reflects a genuine commitment to returning capital rather than empire-building, and insider ownership is negligible, so management has little personal stake in the long-term outcome, and profit capture is only 0.4× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
